(b) THEN ONE Markdown table consistent with the Lock: - [Source Word] | [Morphology] | [Reference Equivalent] | [Contextual Definition] | [Grammatical Role] Source Text: 25 così l'animo mio, ch'ancor fuggiva, 26 si volse a retro a rimirar lo passo 27 che non lasciò già mai persona viva. Reference Translation (provided): so did my soul, which still was flying, turn back to look again upon the pass which never had a living person left.

**Step 1 – Interpretation Lock (one bullet per source line)**
- **Line 25** – *“così l'animo mio, ch'ancor fuggiva,”* ⇒ **Locked Meaning:** The speaker’s soul (*l’animo mio*) is in a continuing state of flight (*fuggiva*) at the moment being described; the adverb *così* signals that this condition follows from the previous narrative clause.
- **Line 26** – *“si volse a retro a rimirar lo passo”* ⇒ **Locked Meaning:** The soul performs a reflexive backward turn (*si volse a retro*) and directs its gaze toward the pass (*lo passo*) with the purpose of looking at it again (*a rimirar*).
- **Line 27** – *“che non lasciò già mai persona viva.”* ⇒ **Locked Meaning:** The pass is characterized by the universal negative proposition: for every entity *p*, if *p* is a living person, then *p* has never left the pass. In other words, **no living person has ever left that pass** (¬∃p [person(p) ∧ alive(p) ∧ left(p, pass)]).
